candidate_relations.reason: The elevated troponin and viral prodrome support myocarditis, but the diffuse inflammatory ECG pattern with PR-segment changes is required for the full myopericarditis diagnosis; viral etiology is not definitively established.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Myocardial inflammatory component with presumed viral etiology; omits pericardial involvement.

candidate_relations.reason: Although chest pain, ST elevation, and troponin elevation can mimic acute coronary syndrome, normal coronary angiography and PR-segment changes support myopericarditis instead.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ischemic coronary syndrome rather than combined myocardial and pericardial inflammation.

candidate_relations.reason: Troponin elevation supports myocardial involvement, but the ECG findings include ST elevation with PR depression and reciprocal PR elevation in aVR, indicating the additional pericardial component required for myopericarditis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Myocardial component only; omits concomitant pericarditis.
